key_evidence_spans: A 70-year-old Japanese man presented with dysphagia and was diagnosed with T3N0M0 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
Enterobacter cloacae was cultured from the wound
MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5
On postoperative day 4, cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge appeared
He developed worsening low back pain and fever (38.2 °C)
Examination revealed lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss
